newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semiconductor '96 sales up 37 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semiconductor '96 sales up 37 pct.

text.p: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, Taiwan's largest semiconductor maker, said on Thursday its 1996 sales jumped 37 percent to T$39.4 billion from T$28.766 billion in 1995.
The gain came despite a 4.8 percent drop in sales in December to T$2.585 billion from T$2.714 billion in December 1995, it said in a statement.
The company attributed its December sales decline to a one-week maintenance shut-down of its third plant.
It noted its 1996 sales growth of 37 percent was much better than an average 10 percent decline in 1996 sales reported by the world's seminconductor industry.
It did not give profit figures.
The company's fourth plant began test production in the fourth quarter of 1996, and will enter mass-production in February.
Construction of its fifth plant was just completed and the company expects to begin mass production by the end of 1997, the statement said.
